# Storyfolio

Makes one kind of portfolio site: one long scroll that tells one story, carried by one object in 3D that is taken from the person's own work.

This version plans the site and does not build it. It ends when the person has said yes to a storyboard.

## Three stops

Between stops you work by yourself. At each stop the person decides one thing. You go on only when their answer is in the conversation and you have written it into the file.

| Stop | First open | You put to the person | You go on when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Read | `references/reading-a-profile.md` | What you found, as facts to confirm and questions to answer. Nothing else | They have answered, and `docs/story/facts.md` holds their answers |
| 2. Concept | `references/concept.md` | Three concepts, and which you would choose | They have picked one, or told you to pick, and `docs/story/concepts.md` says which |
| 3. Storyboard | `references/storyboard.md` | The script of the whole page | They have said yes to it |

**Your first reply is the first stop, and no more than that.** People ask for the whole plan at once: the idea, the scroll, the colours. Do not give it yet, and say why in a sentence. A plan made now is made from your reading of a resume, and a resume leaves out exactly what a site must not get wrong: whose result a number was, what a title hides, who took a photograph. Once they have answered you will have a better idea, and it will not have to be taken apart.

When the storyboard has its yes, say that building is not in this version, and bring `docs/story/handover.md` up to date.

## Ask or decide

Ask the person when a thing is:

1. a fact only they know,
2. a claim that could embarrass them if it were wrong,
3. taste on what a visitor sees first: the concept, the look, the opening words,
4. anything that publishes, costs money, or shows another person or an employer's work.

Everything else you decide. Write each decision into `docs/story/decided-for-you.md`: what you decided, why, and how to change it.

If the person will not answer, or tells you to decide everything, open `references/asking.md`.

## What you keep

In the person's own folder, so that a later session can go on from the files alone:

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `docs/story/facts.md` | The fact sheet, each fact with where it came from, and the person's answers |
| `docs/story/concepts.md` | The three concepts, which was picked, and why |
| `docs/story/storyboard.md` | The script |
| `docs/story/decided-for-you.md` | What you decided without asking |
| `docs/story/handover.md` | What exists, what the person has said, what is next |

## What holds from the first stop on

- **Nothing about the person is invented.** You know that a number, an employer, a title and a quote are facts. So is a sentence about what was wrong before they came, how often a thing is used, why something happened, or what a project taught them. A sentence like that sounds like writing, and it is a claim. If the fact sheet does not hold it, ask for it or leave it out.
- **A number is used as the person confirmed it,** with what it measures and whose result it is.
- **What is someone else's is asked about before it is planned for:** a photograph a photographer took, a friend's drawing, a quote, an employer's screens, a story with a patient or a client in it.


ARGUMENTS: Plan only, do not build. User wants an award-winning, 3D/scroll-driven portfolio that feels personal (not a template/demo). Source material is in a "material folder" that needs to be located and read. Deliverable: a plan covering concept, scroll narrative section-by-section, content per section, color/type system, mobile/responsive behavior, and additional site requirements.

## Who they are, in their own words

- "Founder & Product Analyst" — headline, `resume.md` line 1, `Profile.csv`.
- Summary (`Profile.csv`): "I make dashboards people actually use. Genomics, banking, and a map of Lisbon rents."
- Based in Lisbon, Portugal.

## Jobs

| Employer | Title | Dates | What he did | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Meridian Bank | Product Analyst | Feb 2024 – present | Dashboards used by 200+ staff. "Improved efficiency by 35%." | resume.md, Positions.csv (agree) |
| Helix Genomics Institute | Data Analyst | Sep 2021 – Jan 2024 | Supported sequencing operations. Reduced reporting time by **40%** (resume) / **60%** (Positions.csv). Contributed to a paper in the *Journal of Genomic Methods*. | resume.md, Positions.csv — **disagree on the figure** |
| Atlantico Telecom | Intern | Jun–Sep 2020 ("summer 2020" per resume) | Churn analysis. | resume.md, Positions.csv (agree) |
| DataTugas | Founder | Oct 2018 – Jun 2020 | No description in either source. | Positions.csv; resume.md lists it under "Leadership" with no detail |

## Education

| School | Degree | Dates | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Universidade do Douro | MSc Data Science | 2020–**2021** (resume) / 2020–**2022** (Education.csv) | **disagree on end year** |
| Universidade do Douro | BSc Economics | 2017–2020 | resume.md, Education.csv (agree) |

## Projects

| Project | What it is | Dates | Figure | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FraudShield | "Real-time fraud detection system." | Jan–Jun 2022 | — | resume.md, Projects.csv. No URL, no description of context (employer project? personal? who else built it?) |
| AutoPilot | "Automation platform for analytics teams." | Mar 2024 – present | — | resume.md, Projects.csv. Overlaps with Meridian job start |
| Lisbon Rent Map | "A map of what a room costs in every parish of Lisbon." | May 2023 – present | **5,000** visitors/month (resume) / **3,000** visitors/month (Projects.csv) | **disagree on the figure**. Has a URL: rentmap.example |

## Awards

- Winner, Health Data Hackathon 2023 (Nov 2023). No description of the project or team in either source.

## What others have said

- Beatriz Lima, Head of the Sequencing Core, Helix Genomics Institute (LinkedIn recommendation, 2024-02-11): "Rafael's dashboards changed how the core plans its week. He is the reason we stopped double-booking the sequencers." — a named, attributed quote; using it means naming her and her employer.

## Skills

SQL, Python, Tableau, Power BI, dbt, Statistics. (Skills.csv — no conflicts)

## What he learned from

Not stated anywhere in the material.

## Pictures, drawings or files

None mentioned anywhere in the material — no screenshots, no photo of Rafael, no demo files, no logos.

---

## Gaps

- No visual material at all: no dashboard screenshots, no photo of Rafael, no screenshot/recording of Lisbon Rent Map, no logo or mark for DataTugas.
- No description of what DataTugas is or does.
- No description of the Health Data Hackathon project.
- No description of what Rafael's own part was in the genomics paper.
- No real contact details — the resume email (`rafael@example.com`) reads as a placeholder.
- No stated context for FraudShield or AutoPilot: built alone or with others, ever used in production, by whom.
- Nothing in the material says what he learned from, or who the site is for.

## Disagreements

1. Helix reporting-time reduction: **40%** (resume) vs **60%** (Positions.csv).
2. MSc Data Science end date: **2021** (resume) vs **2022** (Education.csv).
3. Lisbon Rent Map traffic: **5,000/month** (resume) vs **3,000/month** (Projects.csv).

## To confirm

1. Meridian's "35% efficiency": whose result is this — his alone, or the dashboards/team's? What does "efficiency" measure, and over what period?
2. Helix reporting-time figure: which number is right, 40% or 60%, and what does it measure (time per report? time from data to delivery)?
3. Lisbon Rent Map traffic: which number is right, 5,000 or 3,000, and is it a monthly average or a peak?
4. MSc end date: 2021 or 2022?
5. FraudShield: built where and for whom — Helix, Meridian, DataTugas, or on his own? Did it ever run in production? Who else built it with him?
6. AutoPilot: built at Meridian, or independently? Is anyone else using it? Is it something he can show, or does it touch Meridian's systems/data?
7. DataTugas: what is it — a company, a student group, a side project? What did he himself do there?
8. Health Data Hackathon 2023: what did the winning project do? Was it a team, and what was his part?
9. The genomics paper: was he an author, and what did he contribute?
10. Can Beatriz Lima's recommendation be shown by name and title, and can Helix Genomics / Meridian Bank be named at all, including any screenshots of dashboards built there (likely an employer's screens — needs permission either way)?
11. Is there any visual material anywhere — a screenshot, a recording, a photo of Rafael — for any job or project? If not, what could be made (a redrawn chart, a map detail from Lisbon Rent Map, a portrait)?

## Answers (pending)

Awaiting Rafael's reply.
